messages:
sam: Heads up — after pushing the CUDA 12-based runtime to eu-west GPU pool, we're seeing OOMs and intermittent NCCL timeouts across several nodes. Starting this thread to coordinate.

anya: I repro'd on gpu-eu-24. Container logs show driver/runtime mismatch and NCCL errors. Snippet: 
```
E cuda: libcuda reported driver 510.47, required >=525 for toolkit 12.x
W NCCL: NET/IB : No ports found, retrying
E runtime: failed to load kernel module: unresolved symbol
```

mike: Confirmed. Looks like images were rebuilt with nvcc from CUDA-12 and linked against newer libcxx. Hosts in eu-west still have driver 510.x; CUDA12 requires driver >=525.

dave: That explains the symbol errors. We haven't updated host drivers in eu-west because of the maintenance freeze last quarter. If we force-update drivers we risk reboot storms on the older instance types.

sam: Immediate ask: can we roll back the nodepool to the previous CUDA-11-compatible image for running inference? Also need a canary strategy for future toolkit upgrades.

ops-bot: deploy report — rollback job queued: rollback-runtime-eu-west -> queued (priority: high). 3 tasks will run serially.

anya: Quick mitigation: 1) mark eu-west nodes with label `cuda12-incompatible` and drain non-critical tasks; 2) schedule driver upgrades on a per-subnet basis with small batches.

mike: For images: we should rebuild images with a multi-toolkit strategy (have CUDA-11 and CUDA-12 variants) and add a sanity check in CI to run `nvidia-smi` + small NCCL smoke test against a host image with driver pinned. That would've caught it.

dave: Cost/ops note — rebuilding all CI images and running a large matrix will spike CI credits and storage. Estimate: ~1200 CI-minutes and ~40GB extra image cache for the rollout. Is that OK?

sam: Approve the rebuild cost; prefer to pay for the test matrix over live incidents. Also want a short-term plan: rollback for eu-west, canary driver updates for a tiny subset of instances, and a follow-up to document driver min versions per toolkit.

mike: I'll open a PR adding a `cuda-compat-check` job to the pipeline that runs `./smoke_nccl_test.sh` inside the built image and compares to host `nvidia-smi`. If mismatch detected, fail the release.

anya: Ops plan for tonight:
- drain non-prod pods from nodes labeled `cuda12-incompatible`
- run driver upgrade in 3-node batches (max 1 reboot at a time per rack)
- monitor NCCL errors and pod OOMs for 2 hours post-upgrade

deploy-bot: rollback-runtime-eu-west: started at 1784321055 by sam. Step 1/3: cordon + drain selected nodes.

dave: Note: eu-west has older p-machine kernel (5.4) on some hosts; if driver installers use DKMS we might need to rebuild kernel modules. That could fail on out-of-tree modules. Keep kernel compatibility in the checklist.

sam: Action items: mike -> PR for CI compat check; anya -> ops run tonight and sequence; dave -> inventory host kernels and make list of nodes that need manual intervention; ops-bot -> keep posting progress. We'll regroup in #eng-infra 30m. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: rollback-runtime-eu-west: step 1 complete (3 nodes drained). step 2 queued.

mike: Also adding a short doc in infra runbook: "Toolkit vs Host Driver matrix" with minimum drivers, recommended kernels, and fallback behaviors (pin to CUDA-11 images if host driver < required).

anya: Will add a postmortem entry after we stabilise. For now, prioritise stability over throughput.

sam: Thanks all — keep updates coming in this thread.
